ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Cayman Islands: Proceeds of Crime Act (2019 Revision), Anti-Money Laundering Regulations (2023 Revision), Anti-Money Laundering Guidance Notes (CIMA, 2023), Beneficial Ownership Act (2017 Revision) and Companies Act (2023 Revision); Gibraltar: Proceeds of Crime Act 2015, Criminal Justice Act 2015, Financial Services (Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism) Regulations 2019 (LN 2019/212), and Sanctions Regulations 2020
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access — the Cayman exempted company's beneficial ownership register is maintained at the registered office and is accessible to designated competent authorities (Cayman Islands Monetary Authority, Financial Reporting Authority, and Royal Cayman Islands Police Service) and, under specified international cooperation mechanisms, to His Majesty's Revenue and Customs and UK law enforcement; the register is not publicly searchable

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, and beneficial owners against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, UN Security Council Consolidated List, UK Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation (OFSI) Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Sanctions List (as applied via Gibraltar's Sanctions Regulations 2020), and subsidiary lists of the Cayman Islands Financial Reporting Authority; screening must occur before appointment and is repeated at least quarterly; any potential PEP match requires enhanced due diligence, senior management approval, and a suspicious activity report to the Gibraltar Financial Intelligence Unit or the Cayman Financial Reporting Authority as applicable, consistent with FATF Recommendations 12 and 22.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Cayman Islands General Registry — Companies eRegistry portal (https://www.ciregistry.ky); name clearance for the exempted company is also subject to confirmation through the Gibraltar Companies Registry e-services portal (https://www.companyregistry.gi) where the entity establishes a registered branch or presence in Gibraltar
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All corporate names must be in English using Latin-script alphabetic characters; the name may not be identical or confusingly similar to any name already reserved or registered in the Cayman Islands; the suffix 'Limited', 'Ltd.', 'Corporation', 'Inc.', or 'Limited Liability Company' is mandatory for a Cayman exempted company; accents, diacritic marks, and non-Latin characters are not accepted; a foreign-language name may be adopted only if an exact English transliteration is provided and cleared by the Registrar
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file a written representation to the Cayman Islands Registrar of Companies within 21 days of the refusal notice, citing the specific ground of objection and proposing a variation to dispel similarity or sensitivity; the Registrar must issue a determinative response within 30 days; a further appeal lies to the Grand Court of the Cayman Islands by way of originating motion; if the company will also carry on regulated activity in Gibraltar, an equivalent appeal may be brought under the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014 through the Registrar of Companies and, on further appeal, the Supreme Court of Gibraltar. As a practical alternative, the applicant may reserve a fresh name and re-file at a cost of $75 per new search.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permissible — the Cayman exempted company must appoint a licensed registered office provider in the Cayman Islands, which must maintain a physical, attended address; virtual office arrangements are permitted only with regard to the company's trading back-office and helpdesk operations (e.g., omnichannel customer support infrastructure may be hosted remotely in Gibraltar or elsewhere); the statutory registered office cannot be a virtual-only address, and the registered agent must have a physical presence subject to inspection
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low quantifiable risk for unannounced direct inspection of the exempted company's own premises (estimated <5% annual probability for a non-regulated, low-risk helpdesk SaaS entity); however, the Cayman Islands Monetary Authority and the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission may conduct announced or unannounced inspections of the licensed registered agent's records in relation to AML/CFT supervision.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Gibraltar Companies Act 2014 (Cap. 31), Part 11 (Registration of Overseas Companies), ss. 288-307, read with the Cayman Islands Companies Act (2023 Revision), Cap. 22, Part V (Exempted Companies); governed also by the Financial Services (Trust and Company Service Providers) Act 2019 for the licensed registered-office administrator.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies House Gibraltar (H.M. Government of Gibraltar, 119 Main Street) for external registration; Registrar of Companies, Cayman Islands General Registry (Elizabethan Square, George Town) for issuance of the original Certificate of Incorporation of the Exempted Company.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Gibraltar Form OC-1 (Application for Registration as an Overseas Company) together with certified copies of the Cayman Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum and Articles of Association; primary Cayman instrument: Form EX (Application for Incorporation of an Exempted Company) with stamped Memorandum and Articles.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for either the Cayman Exempted Company or its Gibraltar overseas registration. The company may be incorporated with one or more shares of no par value and may commence business immediately upon filing. No escrow deposit or paid-in capital obligation is imposed; issued capital is fixed solely by the board's share-allotment resolution, and the Gibraltar filing requires only a statutory declaration of compliance rather than proof of capital contribution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) that the share subscription of the founding subscribers set out in the Register of Members be and is hereby approved, and the corresponding ordinary shares are allotted, credited as fully paid, in accordance with the Memorandum of Association; (2) that the registered office of the Company be fixed at the office of the licensed registered-office provider in Gibraltar, and that such address be filed with the Registrar of Companies; (3) that the persons named in the Director Register be appointed as first directors, that the person named be appointed Company Secretary, and that the person named be appointed Chief Executive Officer, each to serve until removal or the next annual general meeting; and (4) that the directors be and are hereby authorized to execute the Gibraltar overseas-company registration, open corporate and e-money bank accounts, and take all acts necessary to perfect incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cayman Islands General Registry (Corporate Affairs Division) and Gibraltar Companies House name-check service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to three proposed names for the Exempted Company and, separately, the desired external-company display name for Gibraltar. The name must end with 'Limited', must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name, and must not contain restricted words such as 'Trust', 'Bank', or 'Insurance' absent regulatory consent. Upon approval, secure the name reservation receipt.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form
Proposed name list (primary plus two alternates)
Directors' and subscribers' identity details
Consent letter for use of restricted words (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, promptly file the alternate names; a formal objection may be submitted to the Registrar within 14 days under the Companies Act name-change procedure, and a new reservation may be made without re-paying the full incorporation fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Trust and Company Service Provider (TCSP) regulated by the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the TCSP to draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association embodying exempted-company features, including full exemption from Cayman Islands taxation, one or more subscribers, and board powers. Ensure each subscriber executes the documents before a notary public, that consent of the proposed directors is obtained, and that documents are apostilled under the Hague Convention where foreign execution occurs.
required_dossiers: Memorandum of Association (draft and final)
Articles of Association (draft and final)
Subscribers' executed signatures
Directors' and secretary's consents to act
Notarized and apostilled copies of each signatory's passport and proof of address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the Registry queries drafting ambiguities, instruct counsel to file correcting amendments and a written explanation; defective signature pages are re-executed and re-notarized at no additional statutory fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Filing of the Cayman Exempted Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Cayman Islands General Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the stamped Memorandum and Articles of Association together with Form EX and the registered-office consent letter (Cayman Islands). Pay the applicable government fee and, where required, the annual exempted-company fee for the first year. Upon approval the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation of an Exempted Company, which constitutes conclusive evidence of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Form EX signed by the subscriber
Stamped Memorandum and Articles of Association
Registered office consent and address in the Cayman Islands
Consent of the first directors
Statutory declaration of compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected or queried, cure the specific deficiency cited in the Registry's correction notice and re-file within 21 days; the same filing fee is applied to the corrected submission, and an expedited same-day service is available for urgent matters.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies House Gibraltar (electronic submission via e-Services portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form OC-1 attaching certified copies of the Cayman Certificate of Incorporation, certified Memorandum and Articles, particulars of directors and secretary, and the Gibraltar registered-office address supplied by the local TCSP. Execute the statutory declaration of compliance before a Gibraltar notary or commissioner for oaths and pay the registration fee.
required_dossiers: Form OC-1 duly executed
Certified copy of Cayman Certificate of Incorporation
Certified Memorandum and Articles of Association
Register of directors and secretary with personal particulars
Gibraltar registered-office address (issued by the licensed TCSP)
Statutory declaration of compliance
Receipt of fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the Registrar issues a query, respond with the missing certified documentation within 14 days; a Certificate of Registration as an Overseas Company is then issued. A late-filing penalty may be waived on written request showing reasonable cause.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Board Governance and Statutory Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and Company Secretary acting under the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014 and Cayman Companies Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting, adopt the pro-forma First Board Resolution, issue share certificates to the subscribers, and open the statutory registers including the register of members, register of directors, register of charges, and minute book. Retain the common seal if adopted and execute banking resolutions for account opening.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (Cayman)
Gibraltar Certificate of Registration as Overseas Company
First Board Resolution minutes
Share certificates
Register of members and register of directors
Conflict of interest declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Defective minutes are cured by holding a confirmatory board meeting and issuing rectified minutes; any missing statutory register entry is corrected and filed as an amendment without penalty if made within one month.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Data Protection, Beneficial Ownership, and Economic Substance Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Regulatory Authority (GRA) and Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) Compliance Unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as a data controller under the Gibraltar Data Protection Act 2019 (GDPR-aligned) because the helpdesk SaaS business processes customer and end-user personal data. File the beneficial-ownership register with the GFSC Central Register and submit the annual return to the Income Tax Office. Assess whether the economic-substance test applies to the overseas company's Gibraltar activities and, if applicable, file the substance return.
required_dossiers: GRA data-controller registration form
Beneficial ownership register filing (BO-1)
Annual return form to Companies House
Economic substance notification and return (if applicable)
Privacy policy and data-processing inventory
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the GRA or GFSC issues a non-compliance notice, remedy by submitting the outstanding filing with interest or penalty mitigation; an extension of time may be granted on application setting out compliance efforts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Banking, E-Money Account, and Payment-Rail Onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar-licensed banks and e-money institutions; alternatively UK/EMI providers regulated by the FCA under passported MiCA/EMD arrangements
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the corporate KYC pack to the chosen Gibraltar or UK EMI bank to open the operating account and to activate the target payment rails (Stripe Billing and PayPal Business). Provide the Certificate of Good Standing, certified constitutional documents, director register, UBO declaration, and source-of-funds details. Execute the e-money account agreement and complete AML/CFT customer due diligence.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (Cayman)
Gibraltar Certificate of Registration as Overseas Company
Certificate of Good Standing from the Cayman Registrar
Register of directors and UBO declaration
Board resolution authorizing account opening and signatories
Passports, proof of address, and source of funds of all principals
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where enhanced due diligence is triggered, provide additional notarized source-of-wealth statements; upon rejection by one institution, the same KYC pack may be routed to an alternative EMI to avoid a 30-day cooling-off delay.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Gibraltar Regulatory Authority (GRA) – Digital and Data Protection Directorate; no financial-services license is required for pure helpdesk SaaS under the Financial Services Act 2019, but data-controller registration is mandatory.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Data Controller Registration under the Gibraltar Data Protection Act 2019; a Computer Services and Support Business Operating Permit is not separately required for ISIC 6201 activity because the business does not hold customer funds or provide regulated payment services.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: HM Government of Gibraltar – Department of the Environment, Heritage and Climate Change (EECC), Environmental Agency
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 – Low Environmental Risk (Exempt from Full EIA): the activity is purely administrative/cloud-based with no manufacturing or discharge; only an Environmental Registration for premises-based waste operations (including WEEE) is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No direct wastewater discharge or VOC-emission limit applies to software operation; office premises must comply with the Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment (WEEE) Regulations as applied in Gibraltar (Directive 2012/19/EU), maintaining e-waste disposal records for a minimum of five years; any standby generator must comply with emissions thresholds below 100 mg/Nm³ for NOx.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate under the Gibraltar Fire and Rescue Services legislation for the physical office premises; Building Control structural-load clearance under the Building Act 1997 confirming the office floor load capacity and emergency egress; Occupational health clearance and risk assessment under the Health and Safety at Work (Gibraltar) Act 1997 covering workstation ergonomics, electrical safety, and first-aid provision for all helpdesk employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: HM Government of Gibraltar, Income Tax Office (Commissioner of Income Tax), 6 Secretary's Lane, Gibraltar; e-services portal: https://eservices.gibraltar.gov.gi; corporate registration interface: Gibraltar Companies House / Companies Securities and Registrations Agency (CSRA), https://www.csra.gi
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The Cayman Exempted Company, being a non-resident foreign entity, must first register as an overseas company with the CSRA under Sections 385-386 of the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014 (filing certified certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, registered office address in Gibraltar, and details of local authorised representative). Upon branch registration the CSRA issues a Gibraltar Company Number, following which the entity must complete the Income Tax Office (ITO) registration via the e-services portal (Form IT/CO for non-resident companies) to obtain a Gibraltar Tax Identification Number (TIN). If the company has no Gibraltar-source income and no Gibraltar employees, no tax assessment is raised; if it derives Gibraltar-source income or carries on a Relevant Activity within the meaning of the Economic Substance (Companies) Act 2019, it must additionally file the capital/payroll/annual tax return and economic substance notification. All filings may be effected by a licensed fiduciary/tax agent with a Gibraltar-specific power of attorney.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Cayman Exempted Company status is itself a statutory election: under the Cayman Islands Companies Act the company may apply for a Tax Concessions Certificate under Section 6 of the Tax Concessions Act, guaranteeing exemption from all Cayman income, corporate, and capital taxes for 20 years (renewable to 30 years). In Gibraltar no US-style check-the-box election exists; a non-resident company is taxed purely on Gibraltar-source income on a territorial basis and may elect ordinary residence status under the Income Tax Act if it seeks Gibraltar tax residence. UK hybrid mismatch rules (TIOPA 2010, Part 6A, as amended by the Interest and Royalties Deduction and Hybrid Mismatches Act 2018) apply to the ultimate UK-connected owners and may require a defensive election in respect of any Cayman entity characterised as a hybrid; no Gibraltar hybrid-mismatch election is available because Gibraltar does not operate a VAT regime.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Gibraltar: no VAT or GST regime in force; Gibraltar is outside the EU VAT area and levies customs/import duties only on goods. Cayman: no VAT, GST, sales, or services tax; the only indirect charge is import duty on physical goods, which is inapplicable to exported SaaS/helpdesk services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No indirect-tax registration threshold is applicable because neither Gibraltar nor Cayman imposes VAT/GST. The only compulsory registration steps are (i) CSRA branch registration for the foreign company (no monetary threshold) and (ii) Income Tax Office registration for any non-resident trading activity assessed on a territorial basis; employer registration arises only if the Gibraltar branch hires staff. For the Helpdesk SaaS supplied to non-resident customers via Stripe/PayPal, no VAT threshold, turnover threshold, or customs threshold is triggered.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Gibraltar imposes no real-time fiscal clearance, no API-based B2B e-invoicing, and no digital stamping obligation; invoicing is governed by the Companies (Accounts) Act 2014 and general Income Tax record-keeping rules. Cayman imposes no e-invoicing, clearance, or fiscal control mandate. If the group were to establish a separate UK VAT-registered branch, UK Making Tax Digital (MTD) digital-link rules would apply to that branch; EU ViDA/e-invoicing standards may apply only where an EU-established counterparty requires compliant e-invoicing, but no Gibraltar or Cayman fiscal clearance mandate applies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Given the absence of any Gibraltar or Cayman VAT/GST, the cross-border supply of the customer-support helpdesk SaaS is outside the scope of indirect taxation rather than being 'zero-rated': no output tax is chargeable and no input-VAT refund mechanism exists. If the same entity were to trade through a UK VAT-registered establishment, B2B supplies of support services to non-UK customers would fall within the reverse-charge/outside-scope rules of the UK VAT Act 1994 (Schedule 4, para 8 and place-of-supply rules), thereby achieving an economic 0% effective rate; refund substantiation would require valid invoices, contracts, and evidence of customer business status.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Gibraltar/UK Customs Export Declaration (SAD/C88 or electronic declaration) — applicable only to physical goods exports; not required for pure SaaS/helpdesk services
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill — evidence of physical export, if any goods accompany hardware/embedded devices
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT MT103/credit advice evidencing receipt of the export consideration in foreign currency from the non-resident customer
Duly executed SaaS subscription agreement / helpdesk support order form identifying the customer's country, VAT status, and place of establishment
Support delivery logs, IP/geolocation evidence, and server monitoring records substantiating that the helpdesk performance is rendered entirely offshore (outside Gibraltar/Cayman)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: In the UK/Gibraltar sphere, fraudulent or unsupported export zero-rating or outside-scope claims attract penalties under the Value Added Tax Act 1994 ss.60-72 (penalty up to 100% of evaded tax, default surcharge, and personal liability for responsible officers), plus retrospective assessments for up to 20 years where fraud is established. In Gibraltar, misdeclarations affecting customs duties can invoke penalties of up to three times the duty under the Customs Duties Act, and material false statements to the Income Tax Office are treated as tax evasion with criminal sanctions. In Cayman, because no indirect tax exists, the clawback risk converts into economic-substance penalties: a first non-compliance year penalty of CI$10,000 (≈US$12,200), a subsequent-year penalty rising to CI$100,000 (≈US$122,000), possible strike-off/deregistration, and automatic exchange of information with the UK HMRC under the OECD/CARAT network, which in turn may trigger UK CFC or transfer-pricing enquiries.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) - banking and AML/CFT supervisor; Government of Gibraltar, Commissioner of Currency - issuer of the Gibraltar pound (GIP); Bank of England / Prudential Regulation Authority - monetary anchor via the 1:1 GIP/GBP convertibility guarantee; Cayman Islands Monetary Authority (CIMA) - registrar and AML supervisor at the exempted company's domicile. No standalone Gibraltar exchange-control office exists; exchange-control functions are embedded in GFSC licensing and the UK's Balance of Payments reporting obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full current-account and capital-account convertibility for the Cayman Exempted Company. GIP is freely convertible at 1:1 to GBP; USD and EUR are unrestricted for settlement purposes. The entity holds non-resident classification under the Cayman Exchange Control Regulations, permitting unlimited foreign-currency holdings and unconditional repatriation. Profit-remittance hurdles are nil: Gibraltar imposes no withholding or surrender tax on dividend flows from a Gibraltar branch of a non-resident company, and Cayman levies zero tax. The only execution requirements are a certified board resolution, a UBO declaration, and BoP dividend purpose coding at the account bank. No UK NSIA mandatory filing applies to ISIC 6201 (non-mandatory software sector); no GFSC financial-services licence is required for unlicensed helpdesk SaaS activity. The operational caveat is that bank-level BoP codes must disambiguate PSP service receipts (code 2000) from capital injections (code 3910) and dividend outflows (code 9050).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Zero statutory surrender requirement across the Cayman Islands, Gibraltar, and the United Kingdom. No mandatory conversion ratio and no defined repatriation timeline exist; receipts may be retained indefinitely in the original invoicing currency. The only compliance obligations are (i) the receiving bank's FINREP/BoP statistical reporting and (ii) transaction-level source-of-funds documentation under the GFSC AML regime. Stripe/PayPal settlement flows in USD, EUR, and GBP are therefore 100% retentive, and no GFSC or CIMA permit is required.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Gibraltar International Bank Ltd (GIBank) - HM Government of Gibraltar-owned
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational multi-currency account (GIP/GBP, USD, EUR) with Capital Escrow sub-account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Trusted Novus Bank Ltd (formerly Jyske Bank (Gibraltar) Ltd)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational settlement account (GBP/EUR/USD), Capital Escrow sub-account, and attached FX-forward facility
